blocks.content:
Article 324 | Part XV
Chief Election Commissioner + Election Commissioners
Tenure – 6 years / 65 years
Removal – Like Supreme Court Judge
Independent Constitutional Body
State Election Commission handles local elections
State Election Commission handles local elections

items: Frequently tested: Article 324 deals with the Election Commission under Part XV.
Tenure rule: 6 years or 65 years of age, whichever comes first.
Removal condition: Removal process is equivalent to that of a Supreme Court Judge.
Note the distinction: State Election Commission handles local elections, not the Central Election Commission.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Election Commission is governed by Article 324 under Part XV of the Constitution.
It consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
The tenure for members is fixed at 6 years or until reaching 65 years of age.
Removal of office follows the same procedure as a Supreme Court Judge.
Local body elections are managed separately by the State Election Commission.
